sheet-105.description: The northern end of Wildwood Crest in September 1921, drawn on an additional sheet at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The sheet runs from Sunset Lake on the bay side to the Atlantic Ocean, and from Rambler Road at the top to Sumner Road at the bottom. Three avenues run down the sheet, Philadelphia Avenue beside the lake, Pacific Avenue in the middle and Atlantic Avenue nearest the sea, crossed by Rambler, Orchid, Stockton, Stanton, Farragut, Dupont, Sigsbee and Sumner Roads. Park Boulevard enters at the top left beside Sunset Lake, and a short stretch of Philadelphia Avenue continues above Rambler Road toward sheet 33. Beyond Atlantic Avenue a boardwalk is shown laid on the ground, with open beach between it and the ocean. Every block is platted into numbered lots, but building is sparse: scattered frame dwellings and private garages, mostly along Stockton and Stanton Roads. Named buildings are the Breakers Hotel at Atlantic Avenue and Rambler Road and Binders Villa on Stanton Road; a pavilion or boathouse stands on a pier at the edge of Sunset Lake at the top left. Six-inch water pipes run along Rambler, Orchid and Stanton Roads and a twelve-inch pipe along Pacific Avenue, with hydrants marked. An arm of Sunset Lake reaches into the blocks between Philadelphia and Pacific Avenues at Sigsbee and Sumner Roads, drawn over the platted lots, and the blocks below Sumner Road are outlined only.
notes: Philadelphia Avenue is today New Jersey Avenue; Atlantic Avenue is today Seaview Avenue (modern Atlantic and Ocean Avenues lie on land the beach has gained since).
Rambler, Orchid, Stockton and Stanton Roads are today East Rambler, East Orchid, East Stockton and East Stanton Roads; Farragut Road keeps its name.
Dupont, Sigsbee and Sumner Roads are today East Atlanta, East Nashville and East Louisville Avenues; Sumner Road (East Louisville Avenue) junctions sit 7 to 12 m off and were not used as control.
The boardwalk is drawn as laid on the ground beyond Atlantic Avenue.
Breakers Hotel and Binders Villa are the named buildings.

Wildwood Crest, printed sheet 105 of N.J. coast vol. 4, additional sheet Sept. 1921 (stamped Jan 16 1922), 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left (rotation about -47 deg). One part: Rambler, Orchid, Stockton, Stanton, Farragut, Dupont, Sigsbee and Sumner Rds crossed by Philadelphia, Pacific and Atlantic Avs, Park Blvd, Sunset Lake and the boardwalk laid on the ground. 1921 Philadelphia Av is modern New Jersey Avenue and 1921 Atlantic Av is modern Seaview Avenue (the beach has since grown; modern Atlantic and Ocean Avenues lie on later land). Sumner Rd (modern East Louisville Avenue) left out: its junctions sit 7 to 12 m off.
